## **DORA process — how DHCP works**

**1\. Discover** The client has no IP address yet, so it broadcasts a message across the entire network asking if any DHCP server is available. The source IP is 0.0.0.0 since the client doesn't have one yet, and the destination is 255.255.255.255 so every device on the network receives it.

**2\. Offer** The DHCP server responds with an offer. This message contains a suggested IP address for the client, along with the subnet mask, default gateway, and lease time — essentially everything the client needs to get on the network.

**3\. Request** The client replies confirming it wants the offered IP. This is still sent as a broadcast, which serves two purposes — it tells the chosen server to proceed, and it lets any other DHCP servers on the network know their offers were not selected.

**4\. Acknowledge (ACK)** The server sends a final confirmation back to the client. This officially assigns the IP address, and the client can now use it to communicate on the network. The lease timer also starts from this point.
